key_insight: Data reuploading expands a quantum model’s accessible Fourier frequencies in a precisely characterizable way, with expressivity growing polynomially in reupload depth while the underlying frequency directions stabilize after the first layer.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a concrete rule for predicting when added reupload layers can improve quantum neural network capacity, and when a simpler or classically competitive model may be more efficient.
method: Derive the accessible frequency set for an R-reupload quantum data reuploading architecture as a lattice-constrained sumset.
Prove that spectrum directions saturate at R=1, while frequency count scales as Θ(R^m) with lattice rank m.
Use the spectrum size to obtain a Rademacher-complexity capacity bound of order √(|K_R|/n).
evidence_signal: Experiments on regression and classification, using train/test splits, multiple seeds, and matched classical baselines, showed simulated spectra matching theory exactly and mixed performance versus MLPs depending on task dimensionality.
watch_item: Performance is highly sensitive to input-encoding scale, and the QDR degrades on higher-dimensional regression tasks, so encoding design and problem dimension are critical implementation constraints.
paper_title: On the Expressive Power and Capacity of Quantum Data Reuploaders
